title: Cross-SDK contract fuzzer and deterministic stream snapshotter for Redwood API
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Build a cross-language test runner that combines contract fuzzing with deterministic streaming snapshot capture and assertion. The runner will record HTTP and streaming frames from live Redwood API runs (Python, TypeScript, Go SDKs), normalise transient metadata (timestamps, request IDs, token probabilities), and produce compact, deterministic fixtures that can be used for VCR-style replay and for property-based contract assertions. Goals: 1) catch regressions in retry/backoff, streaming frame ordering, and partial-content semantics across SDKs; 2) make fixtures small, readable, and version-controlled; 3) enable CI gates that compare SDK outputs to golden snapshots with configurable tolerance thresholds; 4) provide a utility to fuzz inputs (prompt shapes, function-calling payloads, edge token sequences) to exercise error paths and rare retry scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: A cross-sdk runner exists that can record live sessions from Python/TS/Go SDKs into a normalized fixture format
Fixtures are deterministic: replays against a mock server return byte-identical payloads after normalization steps (modulo allowed tolerances)
CI job that runs contract fuzz cases on PRs and fails when a contract regression is detected
A small catalog (>= 12) of canonical streaming fixtures covering: short/long generation, early cancel, reconnect+resume, retry-after-206 cases, function-calling sequences
Documentation and quickstart for contributors to add new fixtures and run local replays
Performance: recording of a 1k-token streaming session produces fixtures < 1MB after compression and normalization
comments: 2025-02-15 - Ayesha Khan: Kickoff. Discussed combining deterministic snapshotting from ENG-51234 with a new fuzz harness. Decision: canonical fixture format should be newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with per-frame checksums and a small manifest to enable partial validation.

2025-02-18 - Miguel Alvarez: Implemented prototype recorder for Python SDK that captures streaming frames and writes normalized ndjson. Normalization rules: strip timestamps, map request ids to short stable tokens, quantize float probabilities to 3 decimal places.
2025-02-21 - Design feedback (Lina Park): Add a visual differ for streaming frames in Console to aid reviewers. Filing a follow-up design ticket.
2025-02-24 - QA (Jordan Lee): Ran initial fuzz corpus. Found nondeterminism in reconnect semantics for long-running KV-cache sessions; filed ENG-60210 as follow-up dependency.
2025-02-27 - Miguel Alvarez: Added TypeScript runner and adapter for Go. Found a TLS edge where Go client rewrites chunk boundaries; normalization now includes chunk-boundary canonicalization.
2025-03-01 - PM (Rowan Smith): Authorised adding 4 higher-risk fuzz generators to CI with opt-in gate for nightly runs only until flakiness is < 0.5%.

2025-03-02 - Miguel Alvarez: Opened draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-tests/pull/142. Contains recorder, ndjson format spec, and three sample fixtures. Requesting review from runtime and SDK leads.
implementation_notes: Key implementation choices: (1) Use ndjson per frame with a small JSON manifest describing normalization steps; (2) Normalization pipeline implemented in Rust for the recorder binary to keep cross-SDK adapters thin; (3) Replay mock server supports both strict and tolerant modes (checksum vs fuzzy-match thresholds); (4) Fuzzers are property-based (Hypothesis for Python, fast-check for TS, quickcheck for Go) and produce corpus+shrinking outputs to help triage failures; (5) Keep fixtures under 1MB compressed by storing base64-encoded compressed deltas for streaming frames.
